verdict.rationale: Statsig documents its own client and server SDKs, including a JavaScript/React web SDK and on-device evaluation SDKs, and states that evaluation is deterministic, returning the same result across client and server platforms. That covers the backend, web, and consistency parts of the story. A mobile-specific SDK is never explicitly named: the mobile tutorial only targets mobile platforms by rule and then checks the gate with the JavaScript SDK. missing for 10: explicit documentation of official mobile (iOS/Android/React Native) SDKs, a list of supported backend languages, independent or hands-on corroboration of cross-platform consistency.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use official SDKs across my whole stack — backend, web, and mobile — with consistent flag behavior

citations.quote: Given the same user object and the same state of the experiment or feature gate, Statsig always returns the same result, even across different platforms (client or server).
After initialization, both Client and Server SDKs evaluate experiments/gates _without a network request_, and typically in less than 1ms.
Update your app's default function (typically App.tsx or Layout.tsx) so that the StatsigProvider component identifier wraps all child components.
Statsig's client-side On-Device Eval SDKs provide an alternate client-side architecture.
